Using the corrected sum of the last 13 terms:
\[
\frac{13}{2}(2a+12d)=\frac12\cdot \frac{13}{2}(2a+(2n-14)d)
\]
\[
2(2a+12d)=2a+(2n-14)d
\]
\[
2a+24d=(2n-14)d \implies a=(n-19)d.
\]

Now the ratio of the sum excluding the first three terms to the sum excluding the last three terms is \(6:5\):
\[
\frac{S_n-S_3}{S_n-\text{(last 3)}}=\frac65.
\]
With \(a=(n-19)d\),
\[
S_n=\frac n2(2a+(n-1)d)=\frac{3n(n-13)}2d,
\]
\[
S_n-S_3=\frac{3d}{2}(n-3)(n-12),
\]
\[
S_n-\text{(last 3)}=\frac{3d}{2}(n-3)(n-14).
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{(n-12)}{(n-14)}=\frac65,
\]
so
\[
5(n-12)=6(n-14)\implies n=24.
\]

\[
\boxed{24}
\]
